transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Uh... well, I guess I'm just having some trouble at work lately. The main thing is... I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. I know I'm supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews, but I just... keep leaving my desk. So, yeah. That's why I came in.
When you get up from your desk, what's going through your mind? Are you feeling restless or fidgety, or is it more that you can't seem to focus on your work?

Um... I don't know about what's going through my mind, exactly. I guess I do get a bit restless. Like... if I'm stuck in a training or one of those long team meetings, I'm usually bouncing my leg. Or clicking my pen. I just end up shifting around in the chair a lot, even when I'm trying to look focused. So... yeah.
How long have you been experiencing this restlessness and difficulty staying in one place? Has this been going on since childhood, or is this something more recent?

Um... I guess it isn't really a new thing. Looking back... it's been going on since I was a kid. 

In elementary school, my teachers used to write that I was bright, but... I don't know. I always lost my worksheets. And I guess I missed instructions a lot. They usually had to give me reminders just to finish my classwork. So... yeah. Since then.

When you're working on those claim reviews at your desk, do you find it hard to keep your attention on the task itself, or is it more that your body just won't stay still even when your mind is focused?

Um... I guess it's the attention part. 

If people near me start talking about another claim, or... I just remember some random errand I need to run... my attention just kind of slides off what I'm reading. I usually end up having to reread the same section a few times just to get through it. So... yeah. It's hard to keep my focus on it.

When you're reading through those claim reviews and your attention slides away, do you find that you've actually forgotten what you just read, or do you remember it but just got distracted and need to refocus?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess I just... I realize I wasn't actually absorbing it. Like I was looking at the words but... I don't really remember what they said. I just know I have to start over.
Beyond the trouble with focus and staying still, do you find yourself having difficulty organizing your work, keeping track of deadlines, or planning how to tackle a big project?

Um... yeah. I guess so. Especially since my caseload got bigger. 

My claim folders and notes just kind of... end up all over the place. Email flags, too. I just have a hard time figuring out which policy review to tackle first. So... yeah. It gets a bit messy.
Beyond work, have these attention and restlessness issues affected other areas of your life — like your relationships, social activities, or how you manage things at home?

Um... well, it's mostly work that's the problem right now. I guess... my supervisor actually put me on a performance coaching plan recently. 

My claim files are just... they're falling behind. And they've been questioning my accuracy on the reviews. I don't know... I was hoping to get on the senior adjuster track, but now I'm just worried I might lose that chance entirely. So... yeah, it's mostly just work.

When you were in school as a kid, besides losing worksheets and missing instructions, did teachers or your parents ever mention that you were hyperactive, talked a lot, interrupted people, or had trouble waiting your turn?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think anyone ever said that. I was just... quiet, mostly.

You mentioned that your supervisors have been questioning your accuracy on the claim reviews. When you make mistakes on those reviews, is it usually because you're rushing through them, or is it more that you're missing details even when you're trying to be careful?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess... I try to be careful. But then they tell me I missed something. So... I don't know.
Outside of work, do you have trouble keeping your home organized, managing your bills or appointments, or staying on top of personal tasks?
Um... I guess I'm okay with that stuff. I mean, my apartment isn't perfect or anything, but... it's fine. I just set my bills to autopay, mostly. So... no, not really.

You mentioned your apartment is fine and you manage bills okay with autopay. But when you think about things like remembering appointments, keeping track of personal tasks, or staying organized with things at home — do you find yourself having to write things down or set reminders for those, or do they just come naturally to you?
Um... I guess I just put them in my phone. Like, appointments and stuff. It's... just easier that way. I don't really think about it too much.

When you're doing things you enjoy — like hobbies, watching TV, or spending time with friends — do you find it just as hard to focus and stay engaged, or is the attention problem mainly something that happens at work?
Um... I don't know. I guess I'm fine when I'm just... doing my own thing. Like, if I'm watching something or playing a game, it's... it's fine. It's mostly just work stuff that's hard.

You mentioned that things at home are fine and you manage okay with your phone reminders. But thinking back to school — did you have similar trouble keeping track of assignments, organizing your materials, or remembering what you needed to do, even back then?

Um... yeah, I guess. It's... not really a new thing. Like, back in elementary school, my teachers would always write that I was bright, but... I don't know. They said I lost worksheets a lot. Or I'd miss instructions. They usually had to remind me to actually finish my classwork. So... yeah, I guess I did.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong pattern of inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms beginning in elementary school, with current functional impairment in the workplace. Core ADHD symptoms include difficulty sustaining attention on claim reviews, easy distractibility, poor organizational skills, forgetfulness, and motor restlessness (leg bouncing, fidgeting, frequent position changes). While hyperactivity presentation was quieter than typical, the inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive presentations are both present. Symptoms have persisted from childhood into adulthood with documented work performance decline. The pattern is consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation with some hyperactive-impulsive features.
